typeText.title: Text · circle
typeText.detail1: Strings use double quotes and JSON escapes, up to 2000 characters. Empty or whitespace-only text is not filled. Text inputs keep their original whitespace.
typeText.detail2: Sample values drive editor previews. Defaults prefill label forms and apply when a value is omitted. Required text must contain non-whitespace content.

typeNumber.title: Number · diamond
typeNumber.detail1: Numbers must be finite and between −1,000,000,000,000 and 1,000,000,000,000. Inputs can add minimum and maximum limits. Zero is a filled value.
typeNumber.detail2: Use a decimal point; scientific notation is supported. A number has no implicit unit: dimension properties interpret it as millimetres. Missing optional numbers are null, not zero.

typeBoolean.title: Boolean · square
typeBoolean.detail1: Use true and false without quotes. False is a filled value and is valid for required boolean inputs.
typeBoolean.detail2: Numbers and strings are not converted to booleans. Conditions require a present boolean; an optional boolean can be null. Use filled(value) to check presence.

typeImage.title: Image · triangle
typeImage.summary: Uploaded images used by image properties.
typeImage.detail1: Choose or upload an image in the variable sample/default controls or the label form. Bind it to an image object’s image_asset property. Images cannot be interpolated into text.
typeImage.detail2: Source literals use image("64-character asset ID"). IDs identify uploaded assets, not URLs or paths. The current account must be allowed to use the asset. Null clears an image. CSV runs require an explicit cell-to-image mapping.

variables.title: Intermediate variables
variables.summary: Name a reusable calculated value with let.
variables.detail1: Intermediate types are inferred. Names are case-sensitive, start with a letter, and contain up to 40 letters, numbers, or underscores. Names must not conflict with inputs, targets, or reserved language words.
variables.detail2: Declaration order does not matter. References must exist and cannot form a cycle. Intermediate declarations are evaluated even if no output uses them. Keep a potentially invalid expression inside an if branch when it should only run conditionally.

source.title: Source syntax
source.summary: Assignments, expressions, comments, and literal values.
source.detail1: End each declaration or property assignment with a semicolon. Use // for a line comment. Arithmetic, comparisons, and/or/not, parentheses, and the listed functions are supported. This is a small expression language, not JavaScript or Python.
source.detail2: Assign output properties with target.property = expression. Read a property with the same target.property notation inside an expression. References use stable object IDs internally. Each property can be assigned only once.
source.detail3: Code editing preserves comments and formatting when saved. Editing executable logic in Nodes regenerates canonical source; moving nodes or editing disconnected nodes keeps existing source text.
source.detail4: Ctrl/Cmd+Z undoes typing. The template Undo/Redo controls restore committed changes across both editors. Invalid source stays in its draft, leaves the last valid preview intact, and blocks saving. Tab leaves the editor; completion uses Ctrl+Space and Enter.

propertyInputs.title: Property inputs
propertyInputs.summary: Use another property’s logic result as a typed input.
propertyInputs.detail1: Choose a Property target and Property in Add node, then Read property. The read node has a typed output that connects by click, drag, keyboard, or touch. Bind property creates an assignment instead.
propertyInputs.detail2: A read uses the result of the property’s binding, or its saved template value when unbound. Node and statement order do not matter. Dependencies can pass through intermediate variables; cycles, including self-references, are rejected.
propertyInputs.detail3: Automatic text widths include bound content and typography. Positioning expressions read those measurements. Unbound content is the saved text, including any {'{'}{'{'}tokens{'}'}{'}'}. label.width_mm and label.auto_length are read-only.
propertyInputs.detail4: Automatic label length is fitted after logic changes positions or visibility and is unavailable as a logic input. Disable automatic length to read or bind label.length_mm.

layout.title: Layout and automatic length
layout.summary: Resolve text, measure it, position objects, then fit the final label.
layout.detail1: The renderer resolves text content and typography, including their logic bindings, before measuring automatic widths. Positioning logic and distance holders then use those measurements. Finally it fits automatic label length and checks printable bounds.
layout.detail2: Automatic length uses visible objects and obeys media limits. Hidden anchors have zero extent. Geometry still requires positive widths and heights; hide objects with visible = false.
layout.detail3: Automatic text width and automatic label length have disabled assignment inlets. Source assignments to them are rejected. Manual node drafts are retained while automatic sizing is enabled. Queued labels keep their resolved layout and values even if the template later changes.
layout.detail4: Sizing expressions may use inputs and intermediate values, but cannot depend on unmeasured automatic dimensions, including indirectly through another object’s position.

connections.title: Connections and navigation
connections.summary: Connect values by clicking, dragging, or using the keyboard.
connections.detail1: Click an output and an input, in either order, or drag between them. Repeating an existing connection disconnects it. Focus connectors and press Enter/Space for the same interaction. Escape, a blank-canvas click, or selecting the same connector again cancels.
connections.detail2: Text connectors are circles, numbers diamonds, booleans squares, and images triangles. A hexagon represents an untyped absent or generic value; an empty image keeps its triangle. Polymorphic inputs such as Filled accept different types and adopt their connected value’s shape.
connections.detail3: Pan on blank canvas; use the wheel or zoom buttons to zoom. Frame nodes shows the graph. The Node picker frames one node, including on touch screens. Focus a node header and use arrow keys to move it; Shift moves farther.
connections.detail4: Configurable nodes have one Value type control above their inputs. It applies to both If branches or both Equal/Not equal operands. Disconnect the value inputs before changing it. Wires and type changes that would create incompatible inputs or outputs are rejected; null remains an absent value for optional branches and presence comparisons.
connections.detail5: Disconnected sockets use their editable default values. Disconnect removes a wire; Remove node removes that node and its wires. Disconnected anonymous nodes are editor drafts. Named intermediate nodes remain executable declarations.

errors.title: Errors and limits
errors.summary: Invalid types, cycles, missing values, and bounded evaluation.
errors.detail1: A diagnostic marks the source location when available. Fix incompatible types, undefined names, duplicate outputs, or cyclic dependencies before saving. Unknown functions and arbitrary code are rejected.
errors.detail2: Runtime sample errors include missing required values, division by zero, invalid dimensions, and missing assets. Type-correct source can still fail for a particular input; check the preview and sample values.
errors.detail3: Limits include 20 inputs, 64 intermediates, 128 bindings, 512 expression nodes, 32 dependency levels, and 16,384 source characters. Shared graph values can expand to more than one expression when compiled.

exampleConditional.detail1: The title is 12 mm high with a subtitle and 14 mm without one. The subtitle keeps a positive height and is hidden when absent. Replace these names with the inputs and targets in your template.

autoLength.text: Changes how much tape the whole label uses to fit its visible objects, from 10 to 300 mm. It does not resize text boxes. Fixed-size labels cannot use this option.
autoLength.related: To make a text box grow with its text, select the text and open Layout → Fit text box width to content (height when rotated). Both settings can be used together.

autoWidth.title: Fit text box to content
autoWidth.text: Grows or shrinks this text box to fit its current text, including variable values and logic. Text does not wrap in this mode. For rotated text, the fitted dimension is height.
autoWidth.related: Automatic label length adjusts the entire label. Font size controls the maximum letter size; text can still shrink to fit the box’s other dimension.

length.text: The physical length of the whole printed label along the tape. This is calculated when automatic length or a logic binding controls it, and fixed by the media for fixed-size labels.
length.related: An object’s Width and Height only change its own bounding box.

resolution.text: Chooses the printer raster resolution used to render this template. Printer default follows the design destination’s default; Normal or High selects a supported mode explicitly.
resolution.related: Zoom only magnifies the editing canvas. Show print pixels lets you inspect the raster at the selected resolution.

profile.text: Sets the design’s tape width, preview colors and media compatibility. Fixed-label profiles also set the exact label length.
profile.related: This does not install a cartridge. The cartridge used for printing must match the design’s media requirements.

destination.text: Chooses the printer or printer group whose capabilities and printable area are used while designing.
destination.related: The print destination is chosen separately when submitting labels.

visibility.text: Personal templates belong to your account; User group shares with the selected group; Global makes the template available across the installation, subject to permissions. Sharing includes saved revisions.
visibility.related: Visibility does not grant permission to edit the template or use a printer.

clipping.text: Allows rendering when objects extend beyond the printable guides. The parts outside are cut off in the printed result.
clipping.related: This does not move or shrink objects to make them fit. Turn it off to catch out-of-bounds errors.

pixels.text: Shows the device raster instead of the smooth design preview, so you can inspect pixel edges and image dithering. It does not change the print.

snap.text: Snaps canvas dragging and resizing to half-millimetre steps. Use the numeric position and size fields for finer control.

bounds.text: Shows the bounding boxes of unselected objects on the canvas. These guides are not printed.

fontSize.text: The maximum size of the text. The renderer reduces it when needed to fit inside the text box.
fontSize.related: Fit text box to content changes the box’s size instead. Wrap text allows multiple lines within a fixed box.

wrap.text: Allows text to continue on another line when it reaches the box’s width.
wrap.related: Fit text box to content disables wrapping and fits the box to the text instead. Explicit line breaks in the content are still respected.

characterSpacing.title: Character spacing
characterSpacing.text: Adds space between letters. Zero uses the font’s normal spacing; added gaps shrink when the text shrinks to fit.
characterSpacing.related: Padding adds space at the edges of the text box instead of between letters.

lineSpacing.title: Line spacing
lineSpacing.text: Adds space between lines of text. Zero uses normal line spacing; added gaps shrink with the text.
lineSpacing.related: Padding reserves space between the text and the box’s edges.

padding.title: Text padding
padding.text: Reserves space inside the text box at each edge. Less room remains for text; automatic text width includes the left and right padding.
padding.related: Character and line spacing change the gaps within the text. Distance holders set gaps between separate objects.

imageProportions.text: Fits the image inside its box without stretching it. Unused space may remain. Turn this off to stretch the image to the box’s shape.
imageProportions.related: Lock box proportions controls resizing the box itself. Swapping an image, including through logic, does not resize the box.

boxProportions.text: Keeps the box’s current width-to-height ratio when you resize it in the editor. It does not force the box to match the selected image.
boxProportions.related: Keep image proportions prevents stretching the artwork. Fit box to image resets the box to the image’s ratio.

imageScale.text: Scales the image inside its unchanged box. 1 uses the full available width and height; 0.5 uses half of each dimension, centered in the box.
imageScale.related: Keep image proportions still applies. This changes the artwork size, not the box size or its distance-holder spacing.

brightness.text: Adjusts image brightness before black-and-white conversion. 1 leaves it unchanged; lower values darken and higher values lighten it.
brightness.related: Contrast changes the difference between light and dark areas. Threshold decides which tones print as ink.

contrast.text: Adjusts the difference between light and dark areas before conversion. 1 leaves it unchanged; lower values flatten and higher values strengthen contrast.
contrast.related: Brightness shifts overall lightness. Dithering represents remaining shades with dots.

conversion.text: Threshold converts tones directly to black or white. Dithered shading uses patterns of ink dots to represent intermediate shades.
conversion.related: Brightness and contrast apply before conversion. Show print pixels displays the resulting raster.

threshold.text: The cutoff from 1 to 255 for black-and-white conversion. Darker tones print as ink; increasing the cutoff makes more of the image black.
threshold.related: This cutoff is not used for dithered shading.

barcode.text: Code 128 encodes general text and IDs. EAN-13 and EAN-8 are numeric retail codes with a check digit. Code 39 uses a restricted set of uppercase letters, numbers and symbols.
barcode.related: Choose the format your scanner or receiving system expects. Invalid content produces a preview error.

caption.text: Prints the barcode’s human-readable value beneath the bars, including the calculated check digit for EAN codes.
caption.related: Caption size changes the letters beneath the code, not the encoded value.

qrFill.text: Enlarges the QR code to use the available box area. When off, QR modules use whole printer pixels and may leave additional space.
qrFill.related: QR margin reserves clear space inside the box. The minimum scannable module size is still enforced.

qrMargin.text: Reserves clear space on each side of the QR code. Blank adds a four-module border; 0 removes that built-in border.
qrMargin.related: A QR code still needs clear space around it to scan reliably. Box size and margin together determine the code’s available area.

follow.text: Keeps this object a set distance to the right of or below another object as that object moves or changes size. Deleting the followed object leaves this one at its current position.
follow.related: The gap is measured between bounding boxes, including rotation and padding. Logic can also control positions; a controlled position cannot be dragged freely.

gap.text: The space between this object’s bounding box and the followed object’s bounding box, along the chosen placement direction.
gap.related: Text padding and image scale affect artwork inside a box; this gap is measured between the boxes themselves.

variables.text: Define inputs people fill in when making labels. Variable name is the identifier used in content and logic; Field label is the name shown on the form.
variables.related: Sample values preview the design in the editor. Default values prefill new-label forms. Saved preview input sets override samples only for that preview.

minimumLength.text: The minimum number of characters in a nonempty text input. Leave blank for no minimum.
minimumLength.related: Required controls whether the input may be empty. This does not set a text box’s size or the physical label length.

maximumLength.text: The maximum number of characters allowed in a text input, up to the application limit of 2,000. Leave blank to use that limit.
maximumLength.related: This limits input text, not the physical width of the text box or label. Font size and automatic sizing control the printed layout.
